Where an application for public summons is filed because of the loss of a negotiable instrument, the People's Court shall decide whether to accept the application based on evidence such as the stub of the negotiable instrument, a copy of the lost negotiable instrument, the drawer's certificate of issuing the instrument, the applicant's certificate of lawfully obtaining the instrument, the bank's notice of loss report and suspension of payment, and the certificate of reporting the case.

The announcement shall be published in relevant newspapers or other media and shall be posted on the bulletin board of the People's Court on the same day. If there is a stock exchange at the place where the People's Court is located, the announcement shall also be published at that exchange on the same day.
The announcement period shall not be less than sixty days, and the expiry date of the public summons period shall not be earlier than fifteen days after the payment date of the instrument.

If an interested party asserts rights after the expiration of the period for asserting rights but before judgment is rendered, the provisions of Article 228, paragraphs 2 and 3, of the Civil Procedure Law shall apply.

Where an interested party asserts rights, the People's Court shall notify the interested party to present the instrument to the court and notify the applicant for public summons to inspect the instrument within a specified period. If the instrument for which the applicant for public summons applies for public summons is inconsistent with the instrument presented by the interested party, the court shall rule to reject the assertion of rights by the interested party.

If no one asserts rights within the period for asserting rights, or if the assertion is rejected, the applicant shall apply for a judgment within one month from the date on which the public summons period expires. If the applicant fails to apply for a judgment within the time limit, the public summons procedure shall be terminated.
Where a ruling is made to terminate the public summons procedure, the applicant and the payer shall be notified.

From the date of public announcement of the judgment, the applicant for public summons has the right to request payment from the payer in accordance with the judgment.
If the payer refuses to pay and the applicant brings an action with the People's Court, and the action meets the conditions for prosecution specified in Article 122 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court shall accept it.
Cases tried under the public summons procedure may be tried by a single judge alone. If a judgment declares the instrument invalid, a collegiate bench shall be formed for trial.

An application for withdrawal of the application by the applicant for public summons shall be made before the public summons. If the applicant applies for withdrawal during the public summons period, the People's Court may directly rule to terminate the public summons procedure.

A People's Court that notifies a payer to suspend payment in accordance with Article 227 of the Civil Procedure Law shall comply with the provisions on property preservation. If the payer refuses to suspend payment after receiving the notice of suspension of payment, in addition to taking compulsory measures in accordance with Articles 114 and 117 of the Civil Procedure Law, the payer shall still bear the obligation to pay after judgment is rendered.

After a People's Court terminates the public summons procedure in accordance with Article 228 of the Civil Procedure Law, where the applicant for public summons or the claimant brings an action before the People's Court, if the action is brought for a dispute over rights in an instrument, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the place of payment of the instrument or at the domicile of the defendant; if the action is brought for a dispute not involving rights in an instrument, the case shall be under the jurisdiction of the People's Court at the domicile of the defendant.

A written ruling terminating the public summons procedure made in accordance with Article 228 of the Civil Procedure Law shall be signed by the judge and the court clerk and affixed with the seal of the People's Court.

Where an interested party brings an action before the People's Court in accordance with Article 230 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court may try the case under the ordinary procedure as an instrument dispute.

Where an interested party requests the People's Court to revoke a judgment of exclusion of rights in accordance with Article 230 of the Civil Procedure Law, the applicant shall be listed as the defendant.
If the interested party only claims confirmation that he or she is the lawful holder of the instrument, the People's Court shall state in the written adjudication that the judgment of exclusion of rights shall be revoked after the judgment confirming the interested party as the holder of the rights in the instrument is rendered.

A legally effective ruling on the realization of a security interest, a ruling confirming a mediation agreement, or a payment order shall be enforced by the People's Court that made the ruling or payment order or by the People's Court at the same level as the place where the property subject to execution is located.
For a judgment determining that property is ownerless, the People's Court that rendered the judgment shall take the ownerless property into the ownership of the State or a collective.

A legally effective legal instrument submitted by a party for enforcement with the People's Court shall meet the following conditions:
(1) the subject of rights and obligations is definite;
(2) the content of performance is definite.
If the legal instrument determines continued performance of a contract, the specific content of the continued performance shall be specified.

According to Article 234 of the Civil Procedure Law, if a person other than the party raises an objection to the subject matter of execution, the objection shall be raised before the conclusion of the execution procedure for that subject matter.

An objection raised by a person other than the party to the subject matter of execution shall, after review, be handled separately according to the following circumstances:
(1) if the person other than the party does not have rights and interests in the subject matter of execution sufficient to exclude compulsory execution, the objection shall be rejected by ruling;
(2) if the person other than the party has rights and interests in the subject matter of execution sufficient to exclude compulsory execution, execution shall be suspended by ruling.
Within fifteen days from the date on which the ruling rejecting the objection of the person other than the party is served on the person other than the party, the People's Court shall not dispose of the subject matter of execution.

If the person applying for execution and the person subject to execution reach a settlement agreement and then request suspension of execution or withdrawal of the execution application, the People's Court may rule to suspend execution or terminate execution.

If one party fails to perform or fails to fully perform the settlement agreement voluntarily reached by both parties during execution, and the other party applies for execution of the original legally effective legal instrument, the People's Court shall resume execution, but the portion already performed under the settlement agreement shall be deducted. If the settlement agreement has been fully performed, the People's Court shall not resume execution.

For an application for resumption of execution of the original legally effective legal instrument, the provisions of Article 246 of the Civil Procedure Law on the period for applying for execution shall apply. The period for applying for execution is interrupted by the reaching of a settlement agreement during execution, and such period shall be recalculated from the last day of the performance period stipulated in the settlement agreement.

Where a People's Court decides to suspend execution in accordance with Article 238 of the Civil Procedure Law, if the security has a duration, the period of suspended execution shall be consistent with the duration of the security, but shall not exceed one year at most. If the person subject to execution or the surety transfers, conceals, sells, or damages the secured property during the period of suspended execution, the People's Court may resume compulsory execution.

Where execution security is provided to the People's Court in accordance with Article 238 of the Civil Procedure Law, the person subject to execution or another person may provide property security, or another person may provide a surety. The surety shall have the ability to perform the obligations on behalf of the person subject to execution or to bear the compensation liability on his or her behalf.
Where another person provides an execution guaranty, a letter of guaranty shall be issued to the enforcement court, and a copy of the letter of guaranty shall be delivered to the person applying for execution. Where the person subject to execution or another person provides property security, the relevant procedures shall be handled by reference to the relevant provisions of the Civil Code.

If the person subject to execution still fails to perform obligations after the expiration of the period for suspended execution decided by the People's Court, the People's Court may directly execute the secured property or rule to execute the property of the surety; however, execution of the surety's property shall be limited to the portion of property corresponding to the obligations the surety shall perform.

In accordance with Article 239 of the Civil Procedure Law, if, during execution, the legal person or other organization that is the person subject to execution is divided or merged, the People's Court may rule to designate the legal person or other organization after the change as the person subject to execution; if it is cancelled and there is a successor of its rights and obligations under the relevant substantive law, the People's Court may rule to designate such successor as the person subject to execution.

If an other organization is unable to perform the obligations determined in the legal instrument during execution, the People's Court may rule to execute the property of the legal person or natural person who bears obligations to such other organization according to law.

During execution, if the name of the legal person or other organization that is the person subject to execution is changed, the People's Court may rule to designate the legal person or other organization after the change as the person subject to execution.

If a citizen who is the person subject to execution dies, and his or her heirs have not renounced succession, the People's Court may rule to change the person subject to execution, and the heirs shall repay the debts within the scope of the estate. If the heirs renounce succession, the People's Court may directly execute the estate of the person subject to execution.

After the execution of other legal instruments that are, according to law, to be executed by the People's Court is completed, if such legal instrument is revoked according to law by the relevant organ or organization, upon application by a party, the provisions of Article 240 of the Civil Procedure Law shall apply.

If part of the matters adjudicated by an arbitration institution falls under the circumstances specified in Article 244, paragraphs 2 and 3, of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court shall rule that such part shall not be executed.
If the part that shall not be executed is inseparable from the other parts, the People's Court shall rule that the arbitration award shall not be executed.

After the People's Court rules not to execute an arbitration award in accordance with Article 244, paragraphs 2 and 3, of the Civil Procedure Law, if a party raises an execution objection or applies for reconsideration against that ruling, the People's Court shall not accept it. The parties may reach a new written arbitration agreement on the civil dispute and apply for arbitration, or may bring an action with the People's Court.

During execution, if the person subject to execution uses arbitration proceedings to confirm rights in or divide the property sealed, distrained, or frozen by the People's Court in favor of a person other than the party, the execution procedure of the People's Court shall not be affected.
If the person other than the party disagrees, he or she may raise an objection in accordance with Article 234 of the Civil Procedure Law.
A party who requests non-execution of an arbitration award or a notarized debt document shall raise the request with the enforcement court before the conclusion of execution.

The People's Court shall issue an execution notice within ten days after receiving the written application for execution or the written instrument for transferred execution.
In addition to ordering the person subject to execution to perform the obligations determined in the legal instrument, the execution notice shall also notify the person subject to execution to bear the interest on delayed performance or the damages for delayed performance as specified in Article 260 of the Civil Procedure Law.

If a person applying for execution applies to the People's Court for compulsory execution after the limitation period for applying for execution has expired, the People's Court shall accept the application. If the person subject to execution raises an objection to the limitation period for applying for execution, and after review the People's Court finds the objection established, it shall rule not to execute.
If the person subject to execution, after performing all or part of the obligations, requests restitution of execution on the ground that he or she did not know that the limitation period for applying for execution had expired, the People's Court shall not support the request.

Where a person subject to execution, or the legal representative, person in charge, or actual controller of the person subject to execution, must accept investigation and inquiry and refuses to appear without justifiable reasons after being summoned according to law, the People's Court may summon him or her by force.
The People's Court shall promptly conduct investigation and inquiry of the person summoned by force, and the time for investigation and inquiry shall not exceed eight hours; if the circumstances are complex and detention measures may be taken according to law, the time for investigation and inquiry shall not exceed twenty-four hours.
Where the People's Court adopts forcible summons measures outside its jurisdictional area, it may summon the person to the local People's Court, and the local People's Court shall assist.

The People's Court has the authority to inquire into the identity information and property information of the person subject to execution. Units and individuals in possession of the relevant information must handle the matter in accordance with the notice of assistance in execution.

The People's Court shall not dispose of the property subject to execution unless it has been sealed, distrained, or frozen. With respect to bank deposits and other types of property that may be directly deducted and transferred, the People's Court's ruling on deduction and transfer shall concurrently have the legal effect of freezing.

The period for freezing the bank deposits of the person subject to execution by the People's Court shall not exceed one year; the period for sealing or distraining movable property shall not exceed two years; and the period for sealing immovable property or freezing other property rights shall not exceed three years.
If the person applying for execution applies for an extension of the period, the People's Court shall, before the expiration of the period for sealing, distraining, or freezing, handle the procedures for continuing the sealing, distraining, or freezing, and the continued period shall not exceed the period prescribed in the preceding paragraph.
The People's Court may also handle the procedures for continuing the sealing, distraining, or freezing on its own authority.

In accordance with Article 254 of the Civil Procedure Law, where the People's Court needs to auction the property of the person subject to execution during execution, the People's Court may organize the auction itself, or may entrust an auction institution with appropriate qualifications to conduct the auction.
Where the auction is entrusted to an auction institution, the People's Court shall supervise the auction activities.

If auction evaluation requires inspection and examination of the site, the People's Court shall order the person subject to execution and the person obligated to assist to cooperate. If the person subject to execution or the person obligated to assist does not cooperate, the People's Court may carry out the inspection and examination by force.

Where the People's Court needs to sell by private sale the property of the person subject to execution during execution, it may entrust the sale by private sale to a relevant unit or sell the property by private sale directly by itself.
With respect to property sold by private sale, the People's Court or its staff members shall not purchase it.

With the consent of the person applying for execution and the person subject to execution, and provided that the lawful rights and interests of other creditors and the public interest are not harmed, the People's Court may, without going through auction or sale by private sale, directly appraise the property of the person subject to execution and transfer it to the person applying for execution in satisfaction of the debt. With respect to the remaining debt, the person subject to execution shall continue to pay it off.

If the property of the person subject to execution cannot be auctioned or sold by private sale, with the consent of the person applying for execution, and provided that the lawful rights and interests of other creditors and the public interest are not harmed, the People's Court may, after appraising the property, deliver it to the person applying for execution in satisfaction of the debt, or deliver it to the person applying for execution for management. If the person applying for execution refuses to accept or manage it, the property shall be returned to the person subject to execution.

Where an auction is concluded or a ruling is made to offset a debt with property in accordance with statutory procedures, the ownership of the subject matter shall be transferred when the ruling on the conclusion of the auction or the ruling on offsetting the debt is served on the buyer or the creditor accepting the property in satisfaction of the debt.

If the subject matter of execution is a specific thing, the original thing shall be executed. If the original thing has indeed been damaged or destroyed, with the consent of both parties, compensation may be made at appraised value.
If the two parties cannot reach an agreement on compensation at appraised value, the People's Court shall terminate the execution procedure. The person applying for execution may bring another action.

Where another person holds the property or instrument designated for delivery in the legal instrument, and after the People's Court issues a notice of assistance in execution in accordance with Article 256, paragraphs 2 and 3, of the Civil Procedure Law, the person refuses to hand it over, compulsory execution may be carried out, and the matter may be handled in accordance with Articles 117 and 118 of the Civil Procedure Law.
If the property or instrument is damaged or destroyed while in the possession of the other person, the matter shall be handled by reference to Article 492 of this Interpretation.
If the other person claims lawful possession of the property or instrument, he or she may raise an execution objection in accordance with Article 234 of the Civil Procedure Law.

During execution, if the person subject to execution conceals property, accounting books, or other materials, the People's Court may, in addition to dealing with the person in accordance with Article 114, paragraph 1, item (6) of the Civil Procedure Law, order the person subject to execution to produce the concealed property, accounting books, or other materials. If the person subject to execution refuses to produce them, the People's Court may adopt search measures.
Search personnel shall be dressed in accordance with regulations and shall present the search warrant and their work credentials.

During a search by the People's Court, unrelated persons are prohibited from entering the search site. If the search target is a citizen, the person subject to execution or his or her adult family members, as well as personnel sent by the grassroots organization, shall be notified to be present. If the search target is a legal person or other organization, the legal representative or the principal shall be notified to be present. Failure to appear shall not affect the search.
A search of a woman's body shall be conducted by female enforcement personnel.

Where property that shall be subject to sealing or distraint measures according to law is found during a search, the matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 252, paragraph 2, and Article 254 of the Civil Procedure Law.

A search record shall be made for the search, which shall be signed, fingerprinted, or sealed by the search personnel, the person subject to search, and other persons present. If any person refuses to sign, fingerprint, or seal, the refusal shall be recorded in the search record.

Where the People's Court executes a matured claim owed to the person subject to execution by another person, it may make a ruling to freeze the claim and notify the other person to perform to the person applying for execution.
If the other person objects to the matured claim, and the person applying for execution requests compulsory execution of the part objected to, the People's Court shall not support the request. If an interested party objects to the matured claim, the People's Court shall handle the matter in accordance with Article 234 of the Civil Procedure Law.
If the other person denies a matured claim determined by a legally effective legal instrument, the People's Court shall not support the denial.

Where the People's Court needs, during execution, to handle the transfer procedures for property right certificates such as real estate certificates, land certificates, forest right certificates, patent certificates, trademark certificates, and vehicle or vessel licenses, it may handle the matter in accordance with Article 258 of the Civil Procedure Law.

If the person subject to execution fails to perform the obligation to act as determined in a legally effective legal instrument, and the obligation may be performed by another person, the People's Court may select a person to perform on his or her behalf; if laws or administrative regulations impose qualification restrictions on the performance of such obligation to act, the person shall be selected from among those qualified. When necessary, the person to perform on the person's behalf may be determined by bidding.
The person applying for execution may recommend a person to perform on the person's behalf from among those who meet the conditions, or may apply to perform the obligation on his or her own behalf. Whether to permit such performance shall be decided by the People's Court.

The amount of the expenses for performance on behalf of the person subject to execution shall be determined by the People's Court based on the specific circumstances of the case, and shall be prepaid by the person subject to execution within a specified period. If the person subject to execution fails to prepay, the People's Court may compulsorily execute the expenses.
After the performance on behalf of the person is completed, the person subject to execution may inspect and copy the expense list and the main vouchers.

Where the person subject to execution fails to perform a specific act designated by a legal instrument, and such act can only be performed by the person subject to execution, the People's Court may handle the matter in accordance with the provisions of Item 6 of Paragraph 1 of Article 114 of the Civil Procedure Law.
If the person subject to execution still fails to perform within the performance period determined by the People's Court, the People's Court may handle the matter again in accordance with the provisions of Item 6 of Paragraph 1 of Article 114 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Where the person subject to execution delays performance, the interest or compensation for delayed performance for the period of delayed performance shall be calculated from the date on which the period for performance designated in the judgment, ruling, or other legal instrument expires.

Where the person subject to execution fails to perform an obligation other than the payment of money within the period designated by a judgment, ruling, or other legal instrument, regardless of whether a loss has already been caused to the applicant for execution, the person shall pay compensation for delayed performance. Where a loss has already been caused, the person shall compensate the applicant for execution at twice the amount of the loss already suffered; where no loss has been caused, the compensation for delayed performance may be determined by the People's Court according to the specific circumstances of the case.

Where the person subject to execution is a citizen or other organization, after the enforcement proceedings have commenced, other creditors of the person subject to execution who have already obtained execution titles may apply to the People's Court to participate in the distribution if they discover that the property of the person subject to execution cannot satisfy all claims.
Creditors who have a priority right or security interest in the property sealed up, seized, or frozen by the People's Court may directly apply to participate in distribution and assert the right to priority repayment.

To apply to participate in distribution, the applicant shall submit a written application. The application shall state the facts and reasons concerning participation in distribution and the inability of the person subject to execution to satisfy all claims, and shall be accompanied by the execution title.
An application to participate in distribution shall be filed after the enforcement proceedings have commenced and before the enforcement of the property of the person subject to execution is concluded.

In the enforcement of participation in distribution, after deducting enforcement expenses from the proceeds obtained from enforcement and satisfying claims that shall be repaid with priority, ordinary claims shall, in principle, be satisfied in proportion to their respective amounts to the total amount of all claims applying for participation in distribution. After such satisfaction, the person subject to execution shall continue to pay off the remaining debts. If a creditor discovers that the person subject to execution has other property, the creditor may at any time request the People's Court to enforce.

Where multiple creditors apply to participate in the distribution of the property subject to execution, the executing court shall prepare a property distribution plan and serve it upon each creditor and the person subject to execution. If a creditor or the person subject to execution objects to the distribution plan, it or he/she shall submit a written objection to the executing court within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the distribution plan.

Where a creditor or the person subject to execution submits a written objection to the distribution plan, the executing court shall notify the creditors and the person subject to execution who have not raised an objection.
If the creditors and the person subject to execution who have not raised an objection do not raise any opposing opinions within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the notice, the executing court shall, in accordance with the opinions of the objecting person, review and amend the distribution plan and then make the distribution; if any opposing opinion is raised, the objecting person shall be notified. The objecting person may, within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the notice, file an action with the executing court against the creditors or the person subject to execution who raised the opposing opinion as defendants; if the objecting person fails to file an action within the prescribed period, the executing court shall make distribution in accordance with the original distribution plan.
Where distribution is made during the pendency of the action, the executing court shall deposit an amount of money corresponding to the disputed claim.

Where, during enforcement, an enterprise legal person subject to execution falls under the circumstances specified in Paragraph 1 of Article 2 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, the executing court shall, with the consent of one of the applicants for execution or the person subject to execution, rule to suspend the enforcement against such person subject to execution and transfer the relevant materials of the enforcement case to the People's Court at the place of domicile of the person subject to execution.

The People's Court at the place of domicile of the person subject to execution shall, within thirty days from the date of receipt of the relevant materials of the enforcement case, notify the executing court of its ruling on whether to accept the bankruptcy case. If it decides not to accept the case, it shall return the relevant case materials to the executing court.

Where the People's Court at the place of domicile of the person subject to execution rules to accept the bankruptcy case, the executing court shall lift the preservation measures on the property of the person subject to execution. Where the People's Court at the place of domicile of the person subject to execution declares the person subject to execution bankrupt, the executing court shall rule to terminate the enforcement against such person.
Where the People's Court at the place of domicile of the person subject to execution does not accept the bankruptcy case, the executing court shall resume enforcement.

Where the parties do not agree to the transfer of the case to bankruptcy, or the People's Court at the place of domicile of the person subject to execution does not accept the bankruptcy case, the executing court shall, with respect to the proceeds obtained from the realization of property in enforcement, after deducting enforcement expenses and satisfying claims entitled to priority repayment, satisfy ordinary claims in the chronological order of the sealing up, seizure, or freezing of the property during property preservation and enforcement.

Where a creditor requests the People's Court to continue enforcement in accordance with Article 261 of the Civil Procedure Law, the creditor shall not be subject to the limitation period for applying for enforcement as provided in Article 246 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Where the person subject to execution fails to perform the obligations determined in a legal instrument, the People's Court may, in addition to imposing a penalty on the person subject to execution, include the person in the list of dishonest persons subject to execution according to the circumstances, and notify the person's work unit, credit reference agencies, and other relevant institutions of the information that the person subject to execution has failed or incompletely performed the obligations.

Where no property available for enforcement is discovered after a property investigation, the executing court may, upon the applicant for execution's signature for confirmation, or after the executing court forms a collegiate bench to examine and verify the matter and obtains the approval of the president of the court, rule to conclude the current enforcement proceedings.
After the enforcement is concluded in accordance with the preceding paragraph, if the applicant for execution discovers that the person subject to execution has property available for enforcement, the applicant may apply for enforcement again. A re-application shall not be subject to the limitation period for applying for enforcement.

Where enforcement is concluded due to the withdrawal of the application, if a party applies for enforcement again within the limitation period for applying for enforcement as provided in Article 246 of the Civil Procedure Law, the People's Court shall accept the application.

Where, within six months after the conclusion of enforcement, the person subject to execution or any other person commits an act obstructing the subject matter already enforced upon, the People's Court may, upon application, remove the obstruction, and may impose a penalty in accordance with Article 114 of the Civil Procedure Law. Where losses are caused to the enforcement creditor or other persons by the obstructive act, the victim may separately file an action.

A foreigner participating in litigation shall submit to the People's Court his or her passport or other identification documents used to prove his or her identity.
Where a foreign enterprise or organization participates in litigation, the identification documents submitted to the People's Court shall be notarized by the notarization authority of the country where it is located and legalized by the embassy or consulate of the People's Republic of China in that country, or the certification formalities prescribed in the relevant treaties concluded between the People's Republic of China and that country shall be fulfilled.
A person representing a foreign enterprise or organization in litigation shall submit to the People's Court proof that he or she is entitled to participate in litigation as a representative; such proof shall be notarized by the notarization authority of the country where it is located and legalized by the embassy or consulate of the People's Republic of China in that country, or the certification formalities prescribed in the relevant treaties concluded between the People's Republic of China and that country shall be fulfilled.
For the purposes of this Article, the "country where it is located" means the country where the foreign enterprise or organization is registered for establishment, or a third country where the enterprise or organization has completed business registration formalities.

Where, in accordance with Article 271 of the Civil Procedure Law and Article 521 of this Interpretation, notarization and legalization formalities need to be completed, but the country where a foreign party is located has not established diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China, the documents may be notarized by the notarization authority of that country, legalized by the embassy or consulate of a third country that has diplomatic relations with the People's Republic of China and is stationed in that country, and then forwarded to the embassy or consulate of the People's Republic of China in that third country for legalization.

Where a foreigner, or a representative of a foreign enterprise or organization, signs a power of attorney in the presence of a judge of the People's Court, authorizing an agent to conduct a civil action, the People's Court shall recognize such authorization.

Where a foreigner, or a representative of a foreign enterprise or organization, signs a power of attorney within the territory of the People's Republic of China, authorizing an agent to conduct a civil action, and the power of attorney is notarized by a notarization authority of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall recognize such authorization.

Where a party submits written material in a foreign language to the People's Court, the party shall simultaneously submit a Chinese translation to the People's Court.
If a party has an objection to the Chinese translation, the parties shall jointly entrust a translation institution to provide a translated text; if the parties cannot reach an agreement on the choice of the translation institution, the People's Court shall designate one.

In foreign-related civil litigation, a foreign party may entrust a national of his or her own country as a litigation agent, and may also entrust a lawyer of his or her own country to serve as a litigation agent in a non-lawyer capacity; officials of foreign embassies or consulates in China, upon entrustment by their own nationals, may serve as litigation agents in their personal names, but shall not enjoy diplomatic or consular privileges and immunities in the litigation.

In foreign-related civil litigation, where a foreign embassy or consulate in China authorizes an officer of such embassy or consulate, and the national of that country who is a party is not within the territory of the People's Republic of China, the officer may, in the capacity of a diplomatic representative, engage a lawyer of the People's Republic of China or a citizen of the People's Republic of China, on behalf of such national, to act as an agent in the civil litigation.

In foreign-related civil litigation, if the parties reach an agreement through mediation, a mediation statement shall be prepared and issued. If a party requests a judgment, a judgment may be prepared in accordance with the content of the agreement and served upon the parties.

Parties to a foreign-related contract or to other disputes over property rights and interests may, by written agreement, choose a foreign court at a place that has an actual connection with the dispute, such as the place of domicile of the defendant, the place of performance of the contract, the place where the contract is signed, the place of domicile of the plaintiff, the place where the subject matter is located, or the place where the tortious act is committed, to have jurisdiction.
In accordance with the provisions of Article 34 and Article 273 of the Civil Procedure Law, for cases falling under the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the People's Republic of China, the parties shall not agree to choose a foreign court to exercise jurisdiction, except where the parties agree to choose arbitration.

Where a case is within the jurisdiction of both the courts of the People's Republic of China and a foreign court, if one party commences an action in the foreign court while the other party commences an action in a court of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court may accept the case. After a judgment is rendered, if the foreign court applies or a party requests the People's Court to recognize and enforce the judgment or ruling rendered by the foreign court with respect to the case, such application or request shall not be granted, unless an international treaty concluded or acceded to by both parties provides otherwise.
Where a judgment or ruling of a foreign court has already been recognized by the People's Court, if a party commences an action in the People's Court over the same dispute, the People's Court shall not accept the action.

For a party who has no domicile within the territory of the People's Republic of China, where litigation documents are served by announcement and the party fails to appear in court upon the expiration of the announcement period, the People's Court may render a judgment by default, after which it shall still serve the judgment document by announcement in accordance with Item 8 of Paragraph 1 of Article 274 of the Civil Procedure Law. Where, upon the expiration of three months from the date of service of the judgment document by announcement, the party does not appeal within the thirty-day appeal period, the judgment of first instance shall become legally effective.

Where a foreign national, or the representative or principal responsible person of a foreign enterprise or organization, is within the territory of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court may serve documents on such natural person, or the representative or principal responsible person of the foreign enterprise or organization.
The principal responsible persons of a foreign enterprise or organization include the directors, supervisors, senior officers, and other such personnel of the enterprise or organization.

Where the country where the person to be served is located permits service by mail, the People's Court may serve by mail.
When serving by mail, an acknowledgment of service shall be enclosed. If the person to be served does not sign on the acknowledgment of service but signs on the mail receipt, the service shall be deemed to be effected, and the date of signing shall be the date of service.
If, upon the expiration of three months from the date of mailing, no proof of service is received and it cannot be determined, based on the circumstances, that service has been effected, the service shall be deemed impossible by mail.

Where the People's Court serves litigation documents on a party by announcement in the first instance, it may directly serve litigation documents by announcement in the second instance, unless the People's Court is able to serve by other means than announcement.

The appeal period for appealing against a judgment or ruling of a People's Court of first instance shall, for a party having a domicile within the territory of the People's Republic of China, be the period prescribed in Article 171 of the Civil Procedure Law; and for a party having no domicile within the territory of the People's Republic of China, be the period prescribed in Article 276 of the Civil Procedure Law. Where the appeal periods of all parties have expired without an appeal, the judgment or ruling of the People's Court of first instance shall become legally effective.

The period for the People's Court to examine an application for retrial filed by a party to a foreign-related civil case shall not be subject to the restriction provided in Article 211 of the Civil Procedure Law.

An applicant who applies to the People's Court for enforcement of an award of a foreign-related arbitration institution of the People's Republic of China shall submit a written application, together with the original of the award. If the applicant is a foreign party, the application shall be submitted in the Chinese language.

When the People's Court enforces an arbitral award of a foreign-related arbitration institution by compulsory execution, if the person subject to execution raises an objection on the ground that a circumstance provided in Paragraph 1 of Article 281 of the Civil Procedure Law exists, the People's Court shall examine the objection of the person subject to execution, and shall rule to enforce or not to enforce the award based on the result of the examination.

Where, in accordance with Article 279 of the Civil Procedure Law, a foreign-related arbitration institution of the People's Republic of China submits a party's application for preservation to the People's Court for a ruling, the People's Court may examine the application and rule on whether to grant preservation. If it rules to grant preservation, it shall order the applicant to provide security; if the applicant does not provide security, the court shall rule to dismiss the application.
Where a party applies for preservation of evidence and the People's Court, upon examination, considers that providing security is unnecessary, the applicant may not provide security.

An applicant who applies to the People's Court for recognition and enforcement of a legally effective judgment or ruling rendered by a foreign court shall submit an application, together with the original or a certified true copy of the legally effective judgment or ruling rendered by the foreign court, as well as a Chinese translation. Where the judgment or ruling of the foreign court is a default judgment or ruling, the applicant shall also submit evidentiary documents proving that the foreign court has lawfully summoned the party, unless the judgment or ruling already clearly states such fact.
Where an international treaty concluded or acceded to by the People's Republic of China contains provisions on the submission of documents, such provisions shall apply.

Where a party applies to an intermediate people's court of the People's Republic of China that has jurisdiction for recognition and enforcement of a legally effective judgment or ruling rendered by a foreign court, if the country where the foreign court is located has neither concluded nor jointly acceded to an international treaty with the People's Republic of China, nor established a reciprocal relationship, the court shall rule to dismiss the application, except where the party applies to the People's Court for recognition of a legally effective divorce judgment rendered by a foreign court.
Where an application for recognition and enforcement is dismissed by ruling, the party may commence an action with the People's Court.

Where a party applies to the People's Court for recognition and enforcement of an arbitral award rendered by an ad hoc arbitral tribunal outside the territory of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall handle the matter in accordance with Article 290 of the Civil Procedure Law.

Where a legally effective judgment or ruling rendered by a foreign court or a foreign arbitral award requires enforcement by a court of the People's Republic of China, the party shall first apply to the People's Court for recognition. After the People's Court examines the matter and rules to recognize, the judgment, ruling, or award shall be enforced in accordance with the provisions of Part III of the Civil Procedure Law.
Where a party only applies for recognition and does not simultaneously apply for enforcement, the People's Court shall only examine whether recognition shall be granted and render a ruling accordingly.

The period for a party to apply for recognition and enforcement of a legally effective judgment or ruling rendered by a foreign court or a foreign arbitral award shall be governed by Article 246 of the Civil Procedure Law.
Where a party only applies for recognition and does not simultaneously apply for enforcement, the period for applying for enforcement shall be recalculated from the date on which the ruling of the People's Court on the recognition application takes effect.

For a case involving recognition and enforcement of a legally effective judgment or ruling rendered by a foreign court or a foreign arbitral award, the People's Court shall form a collegiate bench for examination.
The People's Court shall serve the application on the respondent. The respondent may present its opinions.
A ruling made by the People's Court after examination shall become legally effective upon service.

Where a court of a country that has neither a judicial assistance treaty nor a reciprocal relationship with the People's Republic of China directly requests the People's Court to provide judicial assistance without going through diplomatic channels, the People's Court shall return the request and state the reasons.

Where a party uses a judgment or ruling of a court of the People's Republic of China outside the territory of the People's Republic of China and requests a court of the People's Republic of China to certify the legal effect of the judgment or ruling, or where a foreign court requests a court of the People's Republic of China to certify the legal effect of a judgment or ruling, the court of the People's Republic of China that rendered the judgment or ruling may issue a certificate in the name of that court.

Where the People's Court hears civil cases involving the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, the Macao Special Administrative Region, and the Taiwan region, it may apply, by reference, the special provisions on procedures for foreign-related civil litigation.

After this Interpretation is promulgated and comes into force, the Opinions on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China issued by the Supreme People's Court on July 14, 1992 shall be abolished simultaneously; and any judicial interpretation previously issued by the Supreme People's Court that is inconsistent with this Interpretation shall no longer be applied.
